question: Does patching both action-history appearances preserve candidate ordering under the coherent raw-action counterfactual better than patching H3 only?
hypothesis: Persistent patches are closer to the coherent raw-action candidate ordering than H3-only patches; all-block persistent parity is an implementation control, not an independent discovery.
endpoint: H6 official goal costs: archived FP32 visual MSE + 0.1 proprioceptive MSE
arms: native; coherent_raw_h3; all_blocks_h3_donor; all_blocks_persistent_donor; donor_h3_B0..B5; donor_persistent_B0..B5
secondary_pairs: persistent vs H3_only at every site
native vs coherent_raw_h3 once per bank
metrics: tie-aware Spearman rho over all300 costs
intersection count of actual archived top10 elite sets
winner mismatch using minimum candidate ID among exact minimum-cost ties
tie_audits: argmin-set intersection; disjoint minimum sets indicate forced winner change independent of tie breaking
aggregation: 8 whole contexts per task; banks retained separately; no pooling candidates, banks or sites as independent samples; report all case values and descriptive means/counts
uncertainty: No new significance tests or confidence intervals. Individual contexts and complete counts are retained; descriptive findings are restricted to these recorded contexts.
undefined: constant cost ranks yield null Spearman; no dropping cases or selective means; malformed/nonfinite cost arrays abort
selection: No new best-layer selection. Report all seven sites, both banks, both tasks and all three metrics regardless of outcome.
